_what: WHAT THE FRAME CRITIC CAPTURES AND WHAT IT SHOWS THE SEAT — the one file an art session
edits when it moves to a new surface.
The skill (.claude/skills/frame-critic) judges pictures and knows nothing about how a wall
or a floor is composed. That separation is deliberate: everything content-specific lives
here, so the judging layer has nothing in it that a content change can break.
`capture.cmd` is run from the repo root and must write `capture.frame`. The skill refuses if
the file is not rewritten — a frame left over from an earlier build, judged as this one, is
the evidence failure LOOP-PROCESS §2.3 exists to forbid.
`crop` is applied identically to every Yarl frame in the deck — build, plant and approved —
so the crop can never be the tell that identifies one of them. The asset bar has its own,
because it is a different game at a different tile size.
`asset_bar.image` points OUTSIDE the repo and is never copied into it. Bible §13.3:
measurements leave, pixels never do. The seat sees the crop in its own working directory,
which is also outside the repo.
_crop_note: THE ENGINE'S OWN VIEWPORT BAND, not a guess at it. Every capture logs
`grid map: ... view=(0,90)...(750,1001)`, and all three Yarl frames in the wall deck report
the same band. §13.10: instruments take ground truth from the engine's probes rather than
re-deriving it. A cropped-by-eye band is a slow way to make the crop itself a tell.
_asset_bar_note: ⚠ THE CROP WAS WRONG IN TWO DIFFERENT WAYS AND BOTH WERE FOUND BY SEATS CULLING THE BAR.
The bar is the reference the whole comparison rests on: a seat that rejects it for a framing
artefact never makes the comparison it was seated to make.
1. OUT OF BOUNDS. The box inherited from tools/tier1_floors/run_seats.py is
(336, 240, 720, 528) against a source that is 720x504, so the bottom 24 rows fell off
the image. PIL pads that with black and says nothing.
WORST — 'The frame is padded. Content ends at row 239. Rows 240-263 are pure ...'
frame_critic.py now REFUSES an out-of-bounds box rather than padding it.
2. INSIDE THE IMAGE, OUTSIDE THE PICTURE. Shifting the same window up to (336, 216, 720,
504) cleared the padding and still ran into the source's own WHITE PAPER MARGIN — the
example sheet's artwork occupies x 24-695, y 24-479 and everything outside that is white.
WORST — 'There is a pure white (255,255,255) margin occupying x 360-383 ...'
(304, 192, 688, 480) is the same 384x288 window placed wholly inside the artwork. It
shows floor, a wall run, water and props — a fair comparison frame.
STANDING RULE FOR THIS FIELD: after changing it, LOOK AT THE CROP. The out-of-bounds check is
mechanical and exact; 'inside the image but outside the picture' is not something a script
should be trusted to judge, and a weak detector for it would be worse than reading the
verdict — which is how both of these were found.
tools/tier1_floors/run_seats.py still carries the original box. It belongs to an open art
session and this PR does not touch that session's work — but its comparative-seat results
were taken through a padded bar and that is worth knowing before any of them are cited.
_approved_capture_note: STILL NULL, AND NOW FOR A SECOND REASON ON TOP OF THE FIRST.
The first stands: no floor frame has ever been approved as a FRAME. The kept text below
records why the obvious candidate was disqualified.
The second: NO RAFE-APPROVED COMBINED FRAME EXISTS AT ALL. One room with both real surfaces
in it has never been walked. Seeding this field from a wall-lane or a floor-lane capture would
be choosing the baseline my own work is judged against out of a lane that never answered this
question — bible §13.6, a candidate never contributes to its own acceptance bar.
So the deck runs build + bar + plant, three frames, and every verdict records that it ran
without an approved baseline. RAFE'S WALK IS WHAT SEEDS IT: a serviceable-or-better verdict on
the combined build names the first true combined reference, for both surfaces at once.
--- kept, the floor lane's original note ---
The obvious candidate was `r18_family.png` (the build at 0c60bc50), because BISECT-GREY.md
quotes that walk approving the material arm. Reading further disqualifies it: THE SAME WALK
CULLED THE FRAME. REPORT.md §9g records the third ruling set as material arm approved, aging
accepted, and 'one defect left, and it is the tops'. An approved ARM is not an approved FRAME.
_surface_note: MOVED FROM floor TO combined, 2026-09-03. Both tier-one surface lanes finished soloing; this
round composes the landed floor and the landed walls into ONE ROOM and judges them together.
This is still the one file a session edits when the critic changes surface, and the skill
itself knows nothing about floors, walls or rooms.
THE DECK DRAWS ITS PLANT BY SURFACE, and `combined` is served by the two WALL culls and by
neither of the three floor ones. That was settled by reading the pictures: every floor cull
carries 3904 magenta pixels, because the wall family did not exist when it was taken, so a
seat handed one in a deck whose build has real walls catches it for the debug colour rather
than for its defect (LOOP-PROCESS §4.2). The morgue records that per entry now.
AXIS `construction`, which selects cement-cap over grey-walls. A whole-room frame is judged
on whether the place reads as built and held; grey-walls' defect is CHROMA, and PR #171 found
that a chroma plant cannot judge craft — two VOIDs. The right image for the wrong question is
not a control, which is the ruling that put axes on the morgue in the first place.
_standing_station_note: THE STANDING STATION IS SAMPLED FROM THE POLYLINE - the player stands ON the route with the
route ahead inside the lamp's delivered pool. Two earlier stations were wrong for the
question they were asked: a one-tile chokepoint has no flank to contrast against, and an
approach station put the route's lit run off to one side. A capture composed around the
PLAYER is not composed around the ROUTE'S VISIBLE PORTION once the lamp is carried.
